data.label: contradicted
data.reason: The source states that on 13 June 2025, the EU Council agreed to extend temporary protection until 4 March 2027, not until 4 March 2028 as claimed in the post.

claims.claim: On 13 June 2025, the EU Council voiced support for extending temporary protection until 4 March 2028 rather than 4 March 2027.

evidence.quote: Today, the Council voiced its unanimous support for a proposal to extend the temporary protection for the more than 4 million Ukrainians fleeing from Russia’s war of aggression until 4 March 2027.
evidence.reason: The source explicitly states the Council supported extension until 4 March 2027, not 4 March 2028.
evidence.title: EU member states agree to extend temporary protection for refugees from Ukraine

claims.explanation: The source states that on 13 June 2025, the Council voiced unanimous support for extending temporary protection until 4 March 2027, not 4 March 2028. There is no mention of support for extending until 4 March 2028. Therefore, the claim that the Council supported extension until 4 March 2028 rather than 4 March 2027 is contradicted by the source.
